levels.name: A1: Breakthrough / Beginner
levels.description: Establish absolute foundational competence: German phonetics, basic syntax, gender rules, core verbs, sentence structure, negation, numbers, and the distinction between Nominative and Accusative cases.

units.title: Alphabet, Pronunciation & German Phonetics
units.description: Master German sounds: Umlauts (ä, ö, ü), the Eszett (ß), consonant blends (ch, sch, sp, st), vowel length rules, and diphthongs (ei, ie, eu).
units.vocabularyTheme: Letters, spellings, international words, greeting sounds

units.title: Greetings, Personal Pronouns & Regular Verb Conjugation
units.description: Learn to introduce yourself, greet formally and informally, use subject pronouns (ich, du, er/sie/es, wir, ihr, sie/Sie), and conjugate regular present-tense verbs.
units.vocabularyTheme: Greetings, origin countries, professions, languages

units.title: Irregular Present Tense Verbs & Auxiliaries (sein & haben)
units.description: Master the irregular backbone of German: sein (to be) and haben (to have), plus stem vowel changes (e→i, e→ie, a→ä).
units.vocabularyTheme: Daily activities, states of being, personal traits

units.title: Nouns, Articles (der/die/das) & Gender Strategies
units.description: Demystify grammatical gender. Learn why every German noun has a biological or grammatical gender, suffix rules (-ung, -heit, -chen), and indefinite articles (ein/eine).
units.vocabularyTheme: Classroom objects, everyday items, house & furniture

units.title: Plural Forms of German Nouns
units.description: Conquer the 5 plural patterns (-e, -er, -en/-n, -s, no ending) and umlaut mutations. Learn the rules that make plurals predictable.
units.vocabularyTheme: Food, groceries, city locations, family members

units.title: German Word Order: The Verb-Second (V2) Rule
units.description: The golden rule of German syntax: the conjugated verb is always in position 2 in statements, regardless of what comes first (inversion).
units.vocabularyTheme: Time expressions, daily routines, transitional phrases

units.title: Forming Questions: W-Fragen & Ja/Nein-Fragen
units.description: Construct open questions with interrogatives (wer, was, wo, wohin, woher, wie, warum, wann) and closed yes/no questions with verb-first syntax.
units.vocabularyTheme: Biographical questions, travel queries, directions

units.title: Negation: 'nicht' vs. 'kein'
units.description: Never confuse negation again: use 'kein' to negate nouns with indefinite or zero articles, and 'nicht' to negate verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and definite nouns.
units.vocabularyTheme: Preferences, dislikes, dietary restrictions, corrections

units.title: Numbers, Time, Dates & Calendar
units.description: Cardinal and ordinal numbers, official 24-hour vs. colloquial 12-hour time (vor/nach/viertel/halb), days, months, and date prepositions (am, um, im).
units.vocabularyTheme: Schedule, appointments, dates, seasons, clock time

units.title: The Cases: Nominative and Accusative
units.description: Understand case as grammatical role: Nominative for subject, Accusative for direct object. Master the change of masculine 'der' to 'den' and accusative personal pronouns.
grammarFocus: Accusative Prepositions (bis, durch, für, gegen, ohne, um)
units.vocabularyTheme: Shopping, food & drinks, hobbies, daily purchases

units.title: Modal Verbs & Dual-Verb Sentence Brackets
units.description: Express ability, obligation, permission, and desire with the 6 modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen, dürfen, sollen, möchten) and place the infinitive at the sentence end.
grammarFocus: Sentence Bracket (Satzklammer: Modal at V2, Infinitive at End)
units.vocabularyTheme: Rules, duties, free-time abilities, doctor's visits

units.title: Separable and Inseparable Verbs
units.description: Understand why German verbs split: stressed separable prefixes (auf-, an-, ab-, mit-, ein-, aus-) migrate to the end of the clause in main sentences, while inseparable prefixes (be-, ver-, zer-, ent-, er-, ge-) never split.
grammarFocus: Prefix Movement in Present Tense & Modal Combinations
units.vocabularyTheme: Daily routines (aufstehen, einkaufen, anrufen, aufräumen)

units.title: The Imperative Mood (Commands & Requests)
units.description: Form direct commands and polite requests for du (informal singular), ihr (informal plural), and Sie (formal), plus polite softening with 'bitte' and 'mal'.
grammarFocus: Stem Vowel Change Exceptions in Imperative
units.vocabularyTheme: Directions, recipes, instructions, classroom commands

units.title: A1 Capstone Review & Mastery Benchmark
units.description: Synthesize all A1 grammar and vocabulary in comprehensive integrative drills, end-of-level evaluation, and certified A1 diagnostic testing.
units.vocabularyTheme: Comprehensive A1 vocabulary integration

levels.name: A2: Elementary / Foundation Builder
levels.description: Expand expressive capability: indirect objects with Dative case, two-way prepositions, past narratives with Perfekt & Präteritum, reflexive verbs, and introductory subordinate clauses.

units.title: The Dative Case: Indirect Objects & Dative Verbs
units.description: Master the third German case: identify who receives the action. Articles (dem/der/dem/den + -n), dative pronouns (mir/dir/ihm/ihr/uns/euch/ihnen/Ihnen), and verbs that strictly govern Dative (helfen, danken, gefallen, gehören, schmecken).
grammarFocus: Word Order with Accusative & Dative Objects
units.vocabularyTheme: Giving gifts, helping, opinions, restaurant compliments

units.title: Two-Way Prepositions (Wechselpräpositionen)
units.description: The golden rule of spatial prepositions (an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen): Wohin? (Motion/Direction) takes Accusative; Wo? (Static Location) takes Dative.
grammarFocus: Akkusativ vs. Dativ Rule (Wohin? vs. Wo?)
Position Verbs vs. Action Verbs (stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, sitzen/setzen, hängen)
units.vocabularyTheme: Furniture, room layout, moving, city orientation

units.title: The Perfekt Tense: Conversational Past
units.description: Speak about the past naturally using haben or sein + Partizip II. Master regular verbs (ge-...-t), irregular verbs (ge-...-en), separable/inseparable participles, and the sein-movement criteria.
units.vocabularyTheme: Past vacations, yesterday's activities, career milestones

units.title: Präteritum of Sein, Haben & Modal Verbs
units.description: Learn when to use the simple past instead of Perfekt in spoken German: war, hatte, and modal past forms (konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte).
units.vocabularyTheme: Childhood memories, past obligations, historical facts

units.title: Reflexive Verbs & Pronouns
units.description: Express actions done to oneself: echte and unechte Reflexivverben (sich freuen, sich waschen, sich interessieren) with accusative and dative reflexive pronouns.
units.vocabularyTheme: Personal feelings, health, hygiene, interests

units.title: Subordinate Clauses: 'weil', 'dass', 'wenn', 'ob'
units.description: German syntax shift: subordinate clauses send the conjugated verb straight to the very end of the clause. Master causal (weil), factual (dass), conditional/temporal (wenn), and indirect (ob) clauses.
grammarFocus: Comma Rules & Inversion in the Main Clause
units.vocabularyTheme: Expressing reasons, conditions, certainty, and doubt

units.title: Comparison of Adjectives & Adverbs
units.description: Compare items and qualities with the comparative (-er + als) and superlative (am -sten), including irregular forms (gern/lieber/am liebsten, viel/mehr/am meisten, gut/besser/am besten).
units.vocabularyTheme: Product comparisons, lifestyle choices, cities, weather

units.title: Adjective Endings: Introduction & Basic Schemes
units.description: Learn the logic of German adjective endings: after definite articles (der/die/das - weak endings) and indefinite articles (ein/eine - mixed endings) in Nominative and Accusative.
units.vocabularyTheme: Clothing, fashion, shopping descriptions, colors

units.title: Possessive Articles across Cases
units.description: Decline possessive determiners (mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, ihr/Ihr) across Nominative, Accusative, and Dative.
units.vocabularyTheme: Family relations, belongings, workplace colleagues

units.title: Combined Pronoun Order & Double Objects
units.description: What happens when both an accusative object and a dative object appear in one sentence? Master the rule: noun dative precedes noun accusative, but pronoun accusative precedes pronoun dative.
grammarFocus: Object Word Order (Dativ vor Akkusativ bei Nomen)
Pronoun Rule (Akkusativ vor Dativ bei Pronomen)
units.vocabularyTheme: Giving, sending, explaining, office communications

levels.name: B1: Intermediate / Independent Speaker
levels.description: Attain conversational fluency and grammatical independence: full adjective declension, genitive, narrative past (Präteritum), Konjunktiv II, passive voice, relative clauses, and infinitive constructions.

units.title: Complete Adjective Declension (All 3 Schemes across 4 Cases)
units.description: Master the complete matrix: Weak declension (after der/die/das), Mixed declension (after ein/kein/possessive), and Strong declension (no article preceding).
units.vocabularyTheme: Art, architecture, descriptions of nature and people

units.title: The Genitive Case & Genitive Prepositions
units.description: The fourth case: expressing possession, relationship, and academic phrasing with des/der/des/der + -(e)s, plus prepositions: wegen, während, trotz, (an)statt.
grammarFocus: Dative Colloquial Replacement vs. Written Genitive
units.vocabularyTheme: News reports, legal contexts, formal announcements

units.title: The Narrative Past (Präteritum) of Full Verbs
units.description: Read German novels, news, and official accounts comfortably: regular weak verb endings (-te, -test, -te...) and strong irregular ablaut changes (ging, kam, sah, schrieb).
grammarFocus: Stylistic Use: Spoken Perfekt vs. Written Präteritum
units.vocabularyTheme: Biographies, historical chronicles, literary excerpts

units.title: Plusquamperfekt & Temporal Subordinating Connectors
units.description: Express events that occurred before another past event using hatte/war + Partizip II, connected by 'nachdem', 'bevor', 'seitdem', and 'während'.
units.vocabularyTheme: Investigative reports, timelines, sequencing life events

units.title: Futur I: Future Plans, Predictions & Assumptions
units.description: Use werden + Infinitiv to express firm intentions, future forecasts, and present assumptions ('Er wird wohl krank sein').
grammarFocus: Futur I vs. Präsens with Time Marker
units.vocabularyTheme: Technology trends, future predictions, climate changes

units.title: Relative Clauses (Relativsätze)
units.description: Add detail to nouns using relative pronouns (der, die, das, dessen, deren, denen) in Nominative, Accusative, Dative, and with governing prepositions.
grammarFocus: Prepositional Relative Clauses ('das Buch, über das...')
units.vocabularyTheme: Defining objects, describing people, specialized professions

units.title: Konjunktiv II: Wishes, Politeness & Hypotheticals
units.description: Express unreal situations, polite requests, and daydreaming: würde + Infinitiv, hätte, wäre, and modal forms (könnte, müsste, dürfte, sollte).
grammarFocus: Irreal Conditionals (Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich...)
units.vocabularyTheme: Hypothetical dilemmas, dreams, negotiation, customer service

units.title: Passive Voice: The Process Passive (Vorgangspassiv)
units.description: Shift focus from agent to action: werden + Partizip II across Präsens, Präteritum, and Perfekt, with agent attribution using 'von' (+ Dat) and 'durch' (+ Akk).
units.vocabularyTheme: Manufacturing, scientific discoveries, news reports

units.title: Infinitive Clauses with 'zu'
units.description: Connect ideas without repeating subjects: clauses with 'zu + Infinitiv', fixed constructions (um...zu for purpose, ohne...zu, anstatt...zu), and verb triggers (planen, versuchen, hoffen).
units.vocabularyTheme: Goals, intentions, career plans, resolutions

units.title: Two-Part Connectors (Doppelkonnektoren)
units.description: Elevate your sentence structure: 'sowohl ... als auch', 'nicht nur ... sondern auch', 'weder ... noch', 'entweder ... oder', and 'zwar ... aber'.
grammarFocus: Agreement & Word Order with Two-Part Connectors
units.vocabularyTheme: Nuanced arguments, debates, comparisons of pros & cons

units.title: Verbs with Fixed Prepositions (Verben mit Präpositionen)
units.description: The keystone of intermediate German: verbs that require specific prepositions and cases (warten auf + Akk, träumen von + Dat, sich erinnern an + Akk), plus prepositional adverbs (worauf / darauf).
units.vocabularyTheme: Feelings, relationships, projects, expectations

units.title: Indirect Questions & Complex Subordinate Clauses
units.description: Form elegant polite questions in professional situations ('Könnten Sie mir sagen, wann...'), embed multiple clauses, and avoid word-order traps.
units.vocabularyTheme: Customer service, professional emails, official interviews

levels.name: B2: Upper-Intermediate / Professional Fluency
levels.description: Achieve professional and academic precision: indirect speech (Konjunktiv I), condition/state passive (Zustandspassiv), extended participial attributes, nominalisation, formal letter writing, and debate argumentation.

units.title: Indirect Speech & Konjunktiv I
units.description: Report statements objectively in news and legal contexts using Konjunktiv I forms (er habe gesagt, sie seien informiert), with Konjunktiv II replacements when ambiguous.
units.vocabularyTheme: Press briefings, news reporting, courtroom testimonies

units.title: Passive Variants & Zustandspassiv
units.description: Contrast process with finished state: Zustandspassiv (sein + Partizip II), and passive alternatives (man, sich lassen, sein + zu + Infinitiv, -bar/-lich suffixes).
grammarFocus: Passiversatzformen ('Das lässt sich machen', 'Es ist zu beachten')
units.vocabularyTheme: Technical manuals, regulations, product warranties

units.title: Extended Participial Attributes
units.description: Condense relative clauses into sophisticated pre-nominal modifiers using Partizip I (active/simultaneous) and Partizip II (passive/completed): 'die von dem Ausschuss getroffene Entscheidung'.
grammarFocus: Partizip I (-end) & Partizip II as Attributes
Decentering & Unpacking Extended Attributes into Relative Clauses
units.vocabularyTheme: Academic papers, economic analyses, legal documents

units.title: Nominalisation (Nominalstil vs. Verbalstil)
units.description: Master German official and academic style (Behördendeutsch): convert clauses and verbal actions into dense noun phrases using prepositions (durch, bei, infolge, zur).
grammarFocus: Converting Nebensätze into Prepositional Noun Phrases
units.vocabularyTheme: Official correspondence, government forms, business reports

units.title: Advanced Connectors & Nuanced Sentence Linkage
units.description: Master sophisticated logical transitions: concessive (obwohl, obgleich, wenngleich, trotzdem, dessen ungeachtet), modal (indem, dadurch dass), and consecutive (sodass, infolgedessen, folglich).
grammarFocus: Subordinating vs. Adverbial vs. Coordinating Connectors
Word Order Shifts by Connector Class
units.vocabularyTheme: Academic debate, scientific discourse, analytical essays

units.title: Formal and Academic Register (Sprachregister)
units.description: Distinguish between everyday colloquialisms, standard speech, and elevated academic register (Gehobene Sprache). Choose precise vocabulary over generic terms.
grammarFocus: Precise Verb Substitutions (e.g., darstellen instead of zeigen)
Hedging & Modesty Formulas in Academic German
units.vocabularyTheme: Academic presentations, formal inquiries, higher education

units.title: Professional Correspondence: Formal Letters & Emails
units.description: Draft standard-compliant formal communications: Betreffzeile, formal salutations, structured complaints (Beschwerdebrief), job applications (Bewerbungsschreiben), and polite demands.
grammarFocus: Formal Salutations & Closings (Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, Mit freundlichen Grüßen)
units.vocabularyTheme: Job applications, consumer complaints, administrative petitions

units.title: Argumentation, Debate & Opinion Writing
units.description: Structure convincing German essays and debates (Erörterung): theses, arguments, counter-arguments, synthesis, and transitional rhetoric.
units.vocabularyTheme: Societal debates, environmental policy, digital transformation

units.title: Idiomatic Expressions, Collocations & Metaphors
units.description: Decipher and naturally employ common German idioms (Redewendungen) and metaphorical expressions indispensable for native-level comprehension.
units.vocabularyTheme: Colloquial German idioms, business idioms, cultural expressions

levels.name: C1: Advanced / Mastery Extension
levels.description: Bonus advanced modules for effortless mastery: complex syntax, modal particles, noun-verb collocations (Funktionsverbgefüge), stylistic eloquence, and academic synthesis.

units.title: Complex Syntax & Elliptical Structures
units.description: Master verb-first conditionals without 'wenn' ('Hätte ich das gewusst, wäre...'), concessive inversions, and elliptical clauses for stylistic punch.
units.vocabularyTheme: Literary analysis, editorial journalism, rhetorical speeches

units.title: Modal Particles (Modalpartikeln): Pragmatic Nuance
units.description: The soul of natural German: decipher and employ untranslatable particles that signal attitude and tone: 'ja', 'doch', 'mal', 'halt', 'eben', 'wohl', 'eh', 'schon'.
grammarFocus: Modal Particle Function & Placement in the Mittelfeld
units.vocabularyTheme: Natural conversational debate, negotiation, psychological nuance

units.title: Noun-Verb Collocations (Funktionsverbgefüge)
units.description: The hallmark of C1/C2 German: replacing simple verbs with idiomatic noun-preposition-verb collocations: 'zur Verfügung stellen', 'in Betracht ziehen', 'Kritik üben an'.
grammarFocus: FVG Taxonomy (Causative vs. Inchoative vs. Passive)
units.vocabularyTheme: Politics, diplomacy, enterprise management, high-level policy

units.title: Discourse Markers, Cohesion & Textual Flow
units.description: Weave complex arguments with seamless rhetorical coherence: advance signposting, cataphoric reference, and syntactic cohesion.
units.vocabularyTheme: Monographs, dissertations, executive summaries, keynote addresses

units.title: Advanced Reading, Critical Listening & Nuance Detection
units.description: Interpret irony, subtext, subtle bias, and register shifts in German literature, philosophical essays, and high-level political debates.
units.vocabularyTheme: Philosophy, German intellectual history, cultural commentary
